# Master syllabus

Structure: the 19 sections of the official FREC Course I syllabus (eff. 1/1/2023, V-03). Exam weights are low-confidence fragments from the Candidate Information Booklet (V-02); "est." marks estimates used only to weight mock exams.

## 1. The Real Estate Business

*Section 1: Course Overview — The Real Estate Business · Manual: Not covered by the manual (it maps book chapters 2–19 only) · Exam weight: 1%*

### L01-1 · How US and Florida real estate law is organized

- Type: bridge · Priority: high · ~35 min · Content: full
- Manual: M1 intro (partial)
- Prerequisites: none
- Objectives:
  - O-L01-1-1 (understand) Explain the difference between federal law, Florida statutes, Florida administrative rules, and court decisions, and give one real estate example of each.
  - O-L01-1-2 (recall) Name Chapter 475 F.S., Chapter 455 F.S., and Rule Chapter 61J2 F.A.C. and say what each governs.
  - O-L01-1-3 (understand) Describe in one sentence each what the FREC, the DBPR and the courts do in real estate regulation.
  - O-L01-1-4 (apply) Identify which source of law answers a given exam question (federal, Florida statute, FREC rule, case law).
- Practice questions: 4 · Numbers: —

### L01-2 · The real estate business: sectors, specialties and organizations

- Type: conceptual · Priority: medium · ~25 min · Content: full
- Manual: Not in manual
- Prerequisites: L01-1
- Objectives:
  - O-L01-2-1 (recall) List the five categories of real property use (residential, commercial, industrial, agricultural, special-purpose) and classify examples.
  - O-L01-2-2 (understand) Describe the main real estate specializations (brokerage, appraisal, property management, financing, development/construction, counseling).
  - O-L01-2-3 (recall) Explain that REALTOR® is a trademark of NAR membership, not a license, and distinguish it from the state license.
- Practice questions: 3 · Numbers: —

## 2. License Law and Qualifications for Licensure

*Section 2 · Manual: M1 (book Ch. 2–3) · Exam weight: 6%*

### L02-1 · Who needs a license: the three-part test

- Type: legal · Priority: high · ~30 min · Content: full
- Manual: M1 §Who needs a license
- Prerequisites: L01-1
- Objectives:
  - O-L02-1-1 (recall) State the three elements that require a license: a real estate service, for another, for compensation.
  - O-L02-1-2 (recall) List the real estate services named in Chapter 475 (A BAR SALE and related acts).
  - O-L02-1-3 (apply) Decide whether a person in a scenario needs a license, paying attention to how they are paid.
- Practice questions: 3 · Numbers: —

### L02-2 · Exemptions from licensure

- Type: legal · Priority: high · ~25 min · Content: full
- Manual: M1 §Who needs a license (exempt persons)
- Prerequisites: L02-1
- Objectives:
  - O-L02-2-1 (recall) List the statutory exemptions in s. 475.011.
  - O-L02-2-2 (apply) Recognize when a change in compensation or role removes an exemption (salary vs per-transaction pay; attorney earning a commission).
- Practice questions: 4 · Numbers: —

### L02-3 · Qualifying and applying for a sales associate license

- Type: legal · Priority: high · ~30 min · Content: full
- Manual: M1 §Qualifying and applying; §License categories (mutual recognition)
- Prerequisites: L02-1
- Objectives:
  - O-L02-3-1 (recall) State the applicant requirements (age 18, high school diploma or equivalent, SSN) and what is NOT required (citizenship, Florida residency).
  - O-L02-3-2 (recall) State the 63-hour course, its 2-year validity for taking the exam, and the 75/100 passing score.
  - O-L02-3-3 (understand) Explain how criminal history and false applications are treated, and what happens after a denial.
  - O-L02-3-4 (apply) Apply the mutual recognition rules (nonresident at application, 40-question law exam, 30 to pass).
- Practice questions: 5 · Numbers: N-001, N-002, N-003, N-004, N-005, N-006, N-007

## 3. License Law and Commission Rules

*Section 3 · Manual: M1 (book Ch. 2–3) · Exam weight: 2%*

### L03-1 · FREC and DBPR: structure and powers

- Type: legal · Priority: high · ~25 min · Content: core
- Manual: M1 §FREC and DBPR
- Prerequisites: L01-1
- Objectives:
  - O-L03-1-1 (recall) State FREC composition: 7 members, Governor + Senate, 4 brokers (5 yrs), 1 broker or sales associate (2 yrs), 2 consumer members, one member 60+, 4-year terms.
  - O-L03-1-2 (understand) Distinguish quasi-legislative, quasi-judicial and executive/administrative powers, and which body exercises each.
  - O-L03-1-3 (apply) Answer 'which body does X' questions: DBPR investigates; FREC disciplines; courts imprison and award damages.
- Practice questions: 4 · Numbers: N-020, N-021

### L03-2 · License types, registration, group and multiple licenses

- Type: legal · Priority: medium · ~25 min · Content: core
- Manual: M1 §License categories
- Prerequisites: L03-1
- Objectives:
  - O-L03-2-1 (understand) Distinguish sales associate, broker and broker associate, and what only a broker may do.
  - O-L03-2-2 (understand) Distinguish licensure from registration, and group licenses from multiple licenses.
  - O-L03-2-3 (recall) State the broker path: 24 months active in the preceding 5 years, 72-hour course, broker exam, 60 hours post-license.
- Practice questions: 3 · Numbers: N-014, N-015

### L03-3 · Keeping the license: post-license, renewal, CE and license status

- Type: legal · Priority: high · ~35 min · Content: core
- Manual: M1 §Keeping the license alive; §Status map
- Prerequisites: L03-2
- Objectives:
  - O-L03-3-1 (recall) State the 45-hour post-license requirement and the consequence of missing it (license null and void).
  - O-L03-3-2 (recall) State the 14-hour CE requirement per 2-year renewal (3 Core Law + 3 Ethics + 8 specialty) and the consequence of missing renewal (involuntary inactive).
  - O-L03-3-3 (recall) State the reactivation rules: ≤12 months 14 hours; 12–24 months 28-hour course; >24 months void.
  - O-L03-3-4 (understand) Distinguish active, voluntary inactive, involuntary inactive, suspended, revoked, null and void, and ineffective.
- Practice questions: 6 · Numbers: N-008, N-009, N-010, N-011

### L03-4 · Licensee duties to the DBPR: address, convictions, changing brokers

- Type: legal · Priority: high · ~20 min · Content: core
- Manual: M1 §Keeping the license alive; §Status map
- Prerequisites: L03-3
- Objectives:
  - O-L03-4-1 (recall) State the 10-day address-change notice and the 30-day duty to report a conviction or plea (including nolo contendere).
  - O-L03-4-2 (apply) Recognize that a sales associate cannot perform services between brokers until the change is registered.
  - O-L03-4-3 (recall) State that a sales associate may hold only one license and work for one employer at a time.
- Practice questions: 4 · Numbers: N-012, N-013

## 4. Authorized Relationships, Duties and Disclosure

*Section 4 · Manual: M2 (book Ch. 4) · Exam weight: 7%*

### L04-1 · The three brokerage relationships and the transaction-broker presumption

- Type: legal · Priority: high · ~30 min · Content: core
- Manual: M2 §The three relationships
- Prerequisites: L03-2
- Objectives:
  - O-L04-1-1 (recall) Name the three authorized relationships and state that transaction broker is presumed unless another is established in writing.
  - O-L04-1-2 (understand) Explain why dual agency is illegal in Florida and the lawful alternative for working both sides.
  - O-L04-1-3 (understand) Distinguish a principal (single agent) from a customer (transaction broker / no relationship).
- Practice questions: 3 · Numbers: —

### L04-2 · The duty lists: 3, 7 and 9

- Type: legal · Priority: high · ~35 min · Content: core
- Manual: M2 §The duty lists
- Prerequisites: L04-1
- Objectives:
  - O-L04-2-1 (recall) List the 3 duties owed with no brokerage relationship.
  - O-L04-2-2 (recall) List the 7 transaction-broker duties, including what limited confidentiality protects.
  - O-L04-2-3 (recall) List the 9 single-agent duties and the four that belong only to the single agent (loyalty, obedience, full confidentiality, full disclosure).
  - O-L04-2-4 (apply) Match a described duty to the relationship that owes it.
- Practice questions: 5 · Numbers: N-030, N-031, N-032

### L04-3 · Disclosure notices: timing, transitions, scope and exceptions

- Type: legal · Priority: high · ~30 min · Content: core
- Manual: M2 §Disclosures, transitions
- Prerequisites: L04-2
- Objectives:
  - O-L04-3-1 (recall) State when the Single Agent Notice and the No Brokerage Relationship Notice must be given; transaction broker needs no notice.
  - O-L04-3-2 (understand) Explain the Consent to Transition to Transaction Broker and when it is used.
  - O-L04-3-3 (recall) Define 'residential sale' (≤4 units; unimproved for ≤4 units; agricultural ≤10 acres).
  - O-L04-3-4 (apply) Identify situations where disclosure is not required (represented party, open house, casual encounter, general questions, auctions, appraisals, leases without option, business sales).
- Practice questions: 6 · Numbers: N-033

### L04-4 · Material facts, designated sales associates, and ending relationships

- Type: legal · Priority: high · ~30 min · Content: core
- Manual: M2 §Duties that never go away; §Designated sales associates; §How relationships begin and end
- Prerequisites: L04-2
- Objectives:
  - O-L04-4-1 (apply) Decide whether a fact must be disclosed (latent material defect vs stigma such as death or HIV status).
  - O-L04-4-2 (recall) State the designated sales associate conditions: nonresidential, buyer and seller each with assets of $1 million or more, written request/disclosures.
  - O-L04-4-3 (understand) List how brokerage relationships end and which duties survive termination.
- Practice questions: 4 · Numbers: N-034

## 5. Brokerage Activities and Procedures

*Section 5 · Manual: M3 (book Ch. 5) · Exam weight: 12%*

### L05-1 · Escrow accounts and the deposit clock

- Type: legal · Priority: high · ~35 min · Content: core
- Manual: M3 §Escrow accounts
- Prerequisites: L03-2
- Objectives:
  - O-L05-1-1 (recall) State where escrow may be held and the interest-bearing account consent rule.
  - O-L05-1-2 (calculate) Compute the sales associate's and broker's deposit deadlines (next business day; end of third business day) from a receipt date.
  - O-L05-1-3 (recall) State the broker's personal-funds limits ($1,000 sales; $5,000 property management) and define commingling and conversion.
- Practice questions: 4 · Numbers: N-040, N-041, N-042

### L05-2 · Conflicting demands and settlement procedures

- Type: legal · Priority: high · ~30 min · Content: core
- Manual: M3 §Conflicting demands
- Prerequisites: L05-1
- Objectives:
  - O-L05-2-1 (recall) State the 15-business-day notice and 30-business-day procedure deadlines, and the 90-day mediation limit.
  - O-L05-2-2 (recall) Name the four settlement procedures and when an EDO is available.
  - O-L05-2-3 (apply) Recognize the statutory exceptions (condo buyer cancellation; good-faith financing failure).
- Practice questions: 4 · Numbers: N-043, N-044, N-045, N-046

### L05-3 · Advertising rules

- Type: legal · Priority: high · ~20 min · Content: core
- Manual: M3 §Advertising
- Prerequisites: L05-1
- Objectives:
  - O-L05-3-1 (recall) State that every advertisement must include the registered brokerage name; define a blind ad.
  - O-L05-3-2 (apply) Decide whether an ad (sign, social media, website, team ad) complies.
- Practice questions: 3 · Numbers: —

### L05-4 · Offices, signs, compensation, kickbacks and rental lists

- Type: legal · Priority: medium · ~30 min · Content: core
- Manual: M3 §Offices, signs; §Rental lists, kickbacks
- Prerequisites: L05-1
- Objectives:
  - O-L05-4-1 (recall) State the office and entrance-sign requirements ('Licensed Real Estate Broker').
  - O-L05-4-2 (apply) Decide whether a payment is lawful (unlicensed assistant, gift from customer, rebate to a party, referral between licensees).
  - O-L05-4-3 (recall) State the rental-list refund rules (75% if no rental, full if inaccurate, demand within 30 days).
  - O-L05-4-4 (understand) Explain why commission rates must be negotiated individually (antitrust/price fixing).
- Practice questions: 5 · Numbers: N-047

## 6. Violations, Penalties and Procedures

*Section 6 · Manual: M4 (book Ch. 6) · Exam weight: 3%*

### L06-1 · The complaint process

- Type: legal · Priority: high · ~25 min · Content: core
- Manual: M4 §The complaint pipeline
- Prerequisites: L03-1
- Objectives:
  - O-L06-1-1 (recall) Put the steps in order: complaint → investigation → probable cause → formal complaint → hearing → final order → appeal.
  - O-L06-1-2 (understand) Distinguish informal and formal hearings and who presides.
  - O-L06-1-3 (recall) State the 30-day appeal window to the District Court of Appeal.
- Practice questions: 3 · Numbers: N-053

### L06-2 · Penalties and the violation vocabulary

- Type: legal · Priority: high · ~30 min · Content: core
- Manual: M4 §The penalty menu; §Violation vocabulary
- Prerequisites: L06-1
- Objectives:
  - O-L06-2-1 (recall) State the administrative penalties and limits ($5,000 per violation; suspension up to 10 years; revocation).
  - O-L06-2-2 (recall) State the criminal classifications (unlicensed practice: third-degree felony).
  - O-L06-2-3 (understand) Distinguish fraud, misrepresentation, concealment, false promises, culpable negligence and breach of trust.
  - O-L06-2-4 (recall) State the 5-year record-keeping rule.
- Practice questions: 5 · Numbers: N-048, N-050, N-051, N-052

### L06-3 · The Real Estate Recovery Fund

- Type: legal · Priority: high · ~20 min · Content: core
- Manual: M4 §The Real Estate Recovery Fund
- Prerequisites: L06-2
- Objectives:
  - O-L06-3-1 (recall) State the caps ($50,000 per transaction; $150,000 per licensee) and what is not paid.
  - O-L06-3-2 (apply) Decide who may and may not recover from the Fund.
  - O-L06-3-3 (recall) State the consequence for the licensee (automatic suspension until repaid with interest).
- Practice questions: 3 · Numbers: N-054

## 7. Federal and State Laws Pertaining to Real Estate

*Section 7 · Manual: M5 (book Ch. 7) · Exam weight: 3%*

### L07-1 · Fair housing

- Type: legal · Priority: high · ~35 min · Content: core
- Manual: M5 §Fair housing
- Prerequisites: L01-1
- Objectives:
  - O-L07-1-1 (recall) State the protected classes and when each was added (1866 race; 1968; sex 1974; familial status and handicap 1988).
  - O-L07-1-2 (understand) Define blockbusting, steering and redlining and other prohibited practices.
  - O-L07-1-3 (apply) Apply the exemptions and when they are lost (broker used, discriminatory ad; never for race).
  - O-L07-1-4 (understand) Distinguish reasonable modifications from reasonable accommodations.
- Practice questions: 5 · Numbers: N-060, N-061, N-062, N-063

### L07-2 · ADA, ECOA, HMDA and marketing rules (Do Not Call, CAN-SPAM, fax)

- Type: legal · Priority: medium · ~25 min · Content: core
- Manual: M5 §Telemarketing; §ECOA, ADA
- Prerequisites: L07-1
- Objectives:
  - O-L07-2-1 (understand) Match ADA, ECOA, HMDA and fair housing to their subject (public accommodation, credit, lending data, housing).
  - O-L07-2-2 (recall) State the Do Not Call established-business-relationship windows (18 months after a transaction, 3 months after an inquiry; the FTC rule now says 540 / 90 days).
  - O-L07-2-3 (recall) State the CAN-SPAM opt-out rule (honored within 10 business days).
- Practice questions: 5 · Numbers: N-064, N-065

### L07-3 · RESPA and TILA (TRID)

- Type: legal · Priority: high · ~30 min · Content: core
- Manual: M5 §RESPA and TILA
- Prerequisites: L07-1
- Objectives:
  - O-L07-3-1 (recall) State RESPA's scope (federally related loans, 1–4 residential units) and its kickback prohibition.
  - O-L07-3-2 (recall) State TRID timing: Loan Estimate within 3 business days of application; Closing Disclosure at least 3 business days before closing.
  - O-L07-3-3 (apply) Identify TILA advertising trigger terms and the 3-business-day right of rescission (refinance/home equity on principal residence, not purchase loans).
- Practice questions: 4 · Numbers: N-066, N-067

### L07-4 · Florida Residential Landlord and Tenant Act

- Type: legal · Priority: high · ~25 min · Content: core
- Manual: M5 §Florida Residential Landlord and Tenant Act
- Prerequisites: L07-1
- Objectives:
  - O-L07-4-1 (recall) State how security deposits may be held and the 30-day notice of how they are held.
  - O-L07-4-2 (recall) State the move-out timeline: 15 days to return, 30 days to send a claim by certified mail (or e-mail with a signed addendum), 15 days for the tenant to object.
  - O-L07-4-3 (recall) State the termination notices for tenancies without a specific term: 60 / 30 / 30 / 7 days (current law).
  - O-L07-4-4 (recall) State the landlord's flood disclosure duty for residential leases of 1 year or longer (s. 83.512, since October 2025).
- Practice questions: 6 · Numbers: N-068, N-069, N-070, N-071

## 8. Property Rights: Estates, Tenancies, Condos, Co-ops, HOAs, Timeshares

*Section 8 · Manual: M6 (book Ch. 8) · Exam weight: 8%*

### L08-1 · Freehold estates and the bundle of rights

- Type: conceptual · Priority: high · ~30 min · Content: core
- Manual: M6 §Freehold estates; M7 §bundle of rights
- Prerequisites: L01-1
- Objectives:
  - O-L08-1-1 (recall) Name the rights in the bundle (possession, control, enjoyment, exclusion, disposition).
  - O-L08-1-2 (understand) Distinguish fee simple absolute, fee simple defeasible and life estates.
  - O-L08-1-3 (understand) Explain the life tenant's rights and duties (waste) and distinguish remainder from reversion.
- Practice questions: 4 · Numbers: —

### L08-2 · Leasehold estates, lease types, assignment and sublease

- Type: conceptual · Priority: medium · ~30 min · Content: core
- Manual: M6 §Freehold estates (leasehold); §Leases as instruments
- Prerequisites: L08-1
- Objectives:
  - O-L08-2-1 (understand) Distinguish estate for years, periodic tenancy, tenancy at will and tenancy at sufferance.
  - O-L08-2-2 (understand) Distinguish gross, net, percentage, ground, graduated and index leases.
  - O-L08-2-3 (apply) Decide whether a transfer is an assignment or a sublease and who remains liable.
- Practice questions: 4 · Numbers: —

### L08-3 · Co-ownership: tenancy in common, joint tenancy, tenancy by the entireties

- Type: legal · Priority: high · ~30 min · Content: core
- Manual: M6 §Co-ownership
- Prerequisites: L08-1
- Objectives:
  - O-L08-3-1 (recall) State Florida's defaults: unmarried co-owners with a silent deed = tenancy in common; married couple = tenancy by the entireties.
  - O-L08-3-2 (recall) State the four unities (PITT) and the express survivorship language Florida requires for joint tenancy.
  - O-L08-3-3 (apply) Determine who owns a property after a co-owner dies.
- Practice questions: 4 · Numbers: —

### L08-4 · Florida homestead: creditor protection and transfer restrictions

- Type: legal · Priority: high · ~25 min · Content: core
- Manual: M6 §Florida homestead
- Prerequisites: L08-3
- Objectives:
  - O-L08-4-1 (recall) State the size limits (1/2 acre within a municipality; 160 contiguous acres outside).
  - O-L08-4-2 (recall) List the claims that can still reach a homestead (taxes and assessments, purchase or improvement debt, construction liens; federal liens).
  - O-L08-4-3 (understand) Explain the spouse/minor-child protections (spouse joins in deeds and mortgages; devise restrictions).
- Practice questions: 3 · Numbers: N-080

### L08-5 · Condominiums, cooperatives, timeshares, HOAs and CDDs

- Type: legal · Priority: high · ~30 min · Content: core
- Manual: M6 §Condominiums, cooperatives, timeshares, HOAs
- Prerequisites: L08-1
- Objectives:
  - O-L08-5-1 (understand) Distinguish condominium (real property, unit + undivided share) from cooperative (shares + proprietary lease = personal property).
  - O-L08-5-2 (recall) State the cancellation periods: developer condo 15 days; resale condo 7 days excluding weekends and holidays (since July 2025; older texts 3 business days); timeshare 10 days.
  - O-L08-5-3 (recall) State that an HOA disclosure summary must be given before contract, and the buyer's 3-day voiding right if it was not.
- Practice questions: 7 · Numbers: N-081, N-082, N-083

## 9. Title, Deeds and Ownership Restrictions

- Manual: M7 §Wills, water, and what is part of the land

- Objectives:
